title: Treat ProceduralTerrains teardown rejection as native cancellation

scope.subject: Stop Surface fallback unmount from reporting expected ProceduralTerrains prepare cancellation as a fatal runtime error while preserving immediate GPU/resource disposal

research_summary: Hosted shard evidence shows the existing Surface fallback can unmount while procedural-terrains is still inside prepare(), causing FiniteTerrain.dispose() to cancel the pending operation with the library-defined TERRAIN_DISPOSED error. Reuse the installed procedural-terrains 2.0.5 cancellation contract and the existing R3F effect lifecycle: pass an AbortSignal into terrain preparation, abort and dispose during cleanup, and suppress only TERRAIN_CANCELLED/TERRAIN_DISPOSED rejections that occur after this component initiated teardown. Unexpected failures remain fatal. Do not add a terrain job manager, custom worker scheduler, or delayed resource-retention layer.

sources.finding: React Three Fiber keeps lifecycle work inside the existing Canvas/React component tree; use the current effect/useFrame ownership rather than introducing a parallel renderer or loop.

ProceduralTerrains 2.0.5 uses the caller-owned renderer and loop, exposes idempotent dispose(), accepts cancellation for async operations, and documents TERRAIN_CANCELLED/TERRAIN_SUPERSEDED/TERRAIN_DISPOSED rejection codes.

FiniteTerrain.dispose() marks the instance disposed, increments its revision, and calls _cancelJobs('TERRAIN_DISPOSED', ...); prepare(camera,{signal}) races work against cancellation and therefore rejects by design when teardown occurs during preparation.

search_ladder.conclusion: This is a bounded lifecycle correction inside the already-selected Surface renderer, not a product or terrain-engine replacement.
Keep React Three Fiber as the component/frame lifecycle owner and perform cancellation/disposal in the existing SurfaceTerrain effect cleanup.
Reuse ProceduralTerrains native AbortSignal and coded cancellation/disposal semantics instead of wrapping its asynchronous preparation in a second scheduler.
No extra cancellation helper is needed because the selected subsystem already provides operation cancellation, disposal, and typed error codes.

candidates.name: Existing R3F effect ownership for terrain creation and cleanup
candidates.reason: R3F already supplies the correct mount/unmount and frame-loop boundary; keep that ownership and add only subsystem-native cancellation handling inside the effect.

candidates.name: ProceduralTerrains 2.0.5 AbortSignal plus coded teardown rejections
candidates.reason: The subsystem already defines immediate operation cancellation and idempotent resource disposal; distinguish its expected teardown codes rather than treating them as product failures.

candidates.name: Project-owned terrain job and teardown manager
candidates.source: New project-owned async job registry around ProceduralTerrains
candidates.reason: It duplicates the subsystem's cancellation/disposal state, adds a second lifecycle owner, and can retain GPU work longer than the native immediate teardown path.

decision.rationale: Keep R3F as the only component/frame lifecycle owner and ProceduralTerrains as the only terrain-job/resource owner. On effect cleanup, mark local teardown, abort the native operation, and dispose the terrain immediately. The async task suppresses only TERRAIN_CANCELLED or TERRAIN_DISPOSED when local teardown has already begun; all other preparation errors still reach the runtime guard. This directly closes the hosted race without hiding unexpected failures or delaying GPU release.
decision.fallback: If hosted evidence still shows post-unmount terrain work, inspect ProceduralTerrains diagnostics and worker ownership first; do not add a second scheduler unless the native cancellation contract is proven insufficient.
